clue.text: Lacking neighbours, perhaps, is utterly unimportant

definitions.meaning: read literally, beside an empty space with nobody adjacent
the idiom for something of almost no value or size

explanation.surface: Someone with no neighbours is judged to be of no consequence at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a trivial amount, and read literally it describes having only emptiness alongside.

clue.text: Hard to cut into pastry that's risen? Absolutely

indicators.note: in a down clue, something that has risen is read from the bottom upwards
the letters for hard and to are set inside the pastry word, slicing it open

parts.note: a flan is an open pastry case
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A baker asks whether it is tough to slice a risen pastry and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's risen' turns the whole assembly upwards, as this is a down clue; 'cut into' does the insertion first.
explanation.definitionFit: The British colloquial phrase is an emphatic yes, meaning certainly or very much so.

clue.text: Be replacing Greek historian finally — a kind of racist?

indicators.note: the clue's first word takes the place of a letter in the historian's name
points to the final letter of the name as the one swapped out

parts.note: Xenophon was the Athenian historian of the Anabasis
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question over whether an ancient Greek historian, swapped for someone else, was a bigot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' and 'finally' swap the last N of XENOPHON for BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fears or hates foreigners is a type of bigot, close kin to a racist, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Junk food

definitions.meaning: rubbish or nonsense, as in talking drivel
cow's stomach lining eaten as offal

explanation.definitionFit: The word means worthless nonsense and also the edible stomach lining of cattle.

clue.text: Possibly Benedictine school outside a midlands town

parts.note: a nun may belong to the Benedictine order

indicators.note: the school's name wraps around the letter from the clue's a

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monastic school stands on the edge of an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts ETON round A. NUNEATON is a town in Warwickshire, in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuneaton is a market town in Warwickshire, a county in central England.

clue.text: Into child, mother's put nothing but fruit

indicators.note: the mother word is placed inside the child word

parts.note: a tot is a small child
ma is mother
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A mother feeds her child nothing but fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a tomato is a fruit, the berry of the tomato plant.

clue.text: Payment to improve very defective van Gogh I have

indicators.note: lacking something, so a letter is removed from the painter's name

parts.note: Vincent was van Gogh's first name
contracted to I've

explanation.surface: Someone offers money to touch up a badly flawed van Gogh they own.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter is named by his first name; 'defective' strips the abbreviation for very from it.
explanation.definitionFit: An incentive is a reward offered to encourage better performance, such as a bonus.

clue.text: Mount a hack, keeping horse in the country

indicators.note: in a down clue, to mount is to climb, so the letters read upwards
the a-and-hack letters hold the horse letter inside them

parts.note: a nag or hack is a worn-out horse
H is slang for heroin, which crosswords call horse

explanation.surface: A rider climbs on a hired horse in some land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts H inside ANAG to make ANAHG; 'Mount' reverses it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a West African nation, formerly the Gold Coast.

clue.text: Turn back on green.

parts.note: re means on or concerning
vert is the heraldic term for green

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn around when the light shows green.
explanation.definitionFit: To revert is to return to an earlier state, going back to it.

clue.text: Nervousness as a number near holy city

parts.note: ten is a number
Sion is a variant spelling of Zion, Jerusalem

explanation.surface: Anxiety felt by a number of people approaching Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is a state of mental strain or anxiety.

clue.text: Staff holding stuff to be ropy work

indicators.note: the staff word wraps around the stuff word

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: A rod packed with material becomes a piece of poor work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ropy' here is literal, made of rope, not the British slang for shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Macramé is decorative knotted cordwork, so it is literally work made from rope.

clue.text: In exercise, place behind a tree

indicators.note: the exercise-and-place group comes after the letter from a
the place abbreviation goes inside the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: During PE someone positions themselves behind a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The apple is a common fruit tree of the rose family.

clue.text: Late in the evening we hear you dined, wanting to get thin

parts.note: at ten o'clock is late in the evening

indicators.note: signals the second-person word is taken by its sound, a single letter

parts.note: the word you is pronounced like the letter U
ate is dined

explanation.surface: Someone dining late in the evening is told it won't help them slim.
explanation.definitionFit: To attenuate is to make or become thinner or weaker.

clue.text: Tramp's sadly lost, finding nothing in bad visibility

indicators.note: the shuffled letters and the zero go inside the weather word

parts.note: fog causes bad visibility

indicators.note: taken in the sense of badly, a signal to rework the letters

parts.note: the anagram material
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A tramp, gloomily lost, finds nothing in the fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges the letters of lost before the zero joins them inside the weather word.
explanation.definitionFit: To footslog is to tramp or trudge laboriously on foot.

clue.text: A sign in desert where golden road ends?

indicators.note: the a-and-sign letters go inside the desert word

parts.note: sand stands for desert
a mark is a sign

explanation.surface: A sign standing in the desert marks a road's end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AMARK inside SAND. Flecker's poem 'The Golden Journey to Samarkand' made the golden road to that city famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Silk Road city is celebrated in verse as the end of the golden road.

clue.text: One may have pride in large boat

parts.note: big is large
cat is short for catamaran, a boat

explanation.surface: Someone takes pride in their large boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lions are big cats and live in groups called prides.

clue.text: On treacherous seas, part first from Captain Cook

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of the next word
unreliable and untrustworthy, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram material
a role is a part

explanation.surface: Captain Cook, on dangerous seas, plays the first part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treacherous' rearranges SEAS to ASSE. Captain Cook looks like the explorer; Cook is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To casserole is to cook food slowly in a covered dish.

clue.text: Took part on strange instrument

parts.note: sided means took the part of
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone played a part on an odd instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A side drum is a small double-headed drum, the snare.

clue.text: Bore further interrupts very quiet hi-fi equipment

indicators.note: breaks into, so the boring word sits inside the very quiet letters

parts.note: pp is pianissimo, very quiet in music
to ream is to enlarge a bored hole

explanation.surface: A tedious extra intrudes into some silent sound equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very quiet' is the musical marking pianissimo, written as two P's.
explanation.definitionFit: A preamp boosts a weak signal before the main amplifier in a sound system.

clue.text: One about to enter college seen in line

indicators.note: the one-and-about letters go into the college word

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a college
I is the Roman numeral one
c is circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone about to start college is seen standing in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy is a course of action, as in the party line.

clue.text: Unwell, failed to retain much — water

indicators.note: the failed word holds the water word inside

parts.note: died means failed, as an engine does
seas, as in a great deal of water

explanation.surface: Someone poorly cannot keep much down, even water.
explanation.definitionFit: Diseased means affected by illness, hence unwell.

clue.text: Sad, though having just received one's giro?

definitions.text: though having just received one's giro?
definitions.meaning: literally full of dole; a giro was the British unemployment benefit cheque

explanation.surface: A joke that someone just paid their benefit is still glum.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means mournful, and read as dole-full it is someone flush with benefit money.

clue.text: Finger baked dish full of liquid

indicators.note: the dish word holds the liquid word inside

parts.note: a pie is a baked dish
ink is a liquid

explanation.surface: A finger dipped in a pie brimming with juice.
explanation.definitionFit: The pinkie is the little finger.

clue.text: Say, Don Giovanni's composer breaking boundary

indicators.note: the composer splits the boundary word open

parts.note: a line is a boundary
Jacques Ibert was a French composer

explanation.surface: Mozart, composer of Don Giovanni, is pushing the limits.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites Mozart, but the composer is the Frenchman Jacques Ibert.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Giovanni is the archetypal seducer, a debauchee and womaniser.

clue.text: Old statesman's short article — it's. on some Muslims

indicators.note: cut short, so the statesman's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Edmund Burke was an 18th-century Anglo-Irish statesman
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An old politician's brief piece about clothing worn by Muslims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the final E from BURKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A burka is a full-body covering worn by some Muslim women.

clue.text: Rob's toughness spoken of

indicators.note: the word for toughness is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: steel means strength or toughness

explanation.surface: A man called Rob is talked about for his resilience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken of' turns STEEL into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal is to rob or take without permission.

clue.text: Spaniard's nose put out of joint by leader of rivals

indicators.note: dislocated, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram material

indicators.note: take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A Spaniard's nose is put out of joint by his rivals' leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out of joint' rearranges the letters of nose; the leader of rivals then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Señor is the Spanish title for a man, so it can stand for a Spaniard.

clue.text: Stopping payment here may involve on-screen display

definitions.text: Stopping payment here may involve on-screen display

parts.words: Stopping payment here may involve on-screen display
parts.note: stopping means parking a vehicle, and the payment is a pay-and-display ticket at a machine screen

explanation.surface: Cancelling a payment needs something shown on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a place is where motorists stop and pay, often by pay-and-display machine.

clue.text: Put down phone, as sign engagement's terminated?

definitions.meaning: end a telephone call by hanging up
literally, the betrothal band is taken off

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to hang up a telephone, and literally removing an engagement band.

clue.text: Article attracted wonder that's by Pound, the poet

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
drew means attracted
marvel is wonder
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: A piece drew admiration through its link with Ezra Pound, the poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound looks like Ezra Pound but gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Marvell was a 17th-century English metaphysical poet.
